content.title: About
content.content: Frozen cherries are ripe cherries harvested at peak season and quickly frozen to preserve flavor, aroma, and nutrients. The berries have a bright red color, a sweet‑tart taste, and a firm texture after thawing. They are convenient for cooking, baking, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots, and almonds.
Freezing occurs within minutes of picking, retaining over 90 % of vitamin C.
Cherries are rich in anthocyanins, which give them their deep red color and antioxidant properties.
In Russia, the largest producers of frozen cherries are the Siberian and Far Eastern regions.
Frozen berries are often used as fillings for pies, cupcakes, and ice cream.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Flavonoids in cherries improve vascular function and may lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal blood pressure.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and other micronutrients contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cherries.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Cherries contain natural sugars; people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in those with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frozen cherries can be added to smoothies, yogurts, oatmeal, baked goods, sauces, and ice cream. They can be thawed in the refrigerator or used directly in hot dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store frozen cherries in an airtight bag or container at –18 °C. After thawing, consume within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.

pasta-whole-grain-with-cream-sauce-and-a.title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta is made from whole wheat flour, retaining the bran and germ. Combined with a creamy sauce and added vegetables, it creates a nutritious home‑cooked dish rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta keeps the bran and germ, boosting its nutritional value compared with refined white pasta.
Cream sauces are often based on dairy cream, milk, or soft cheese, giving the dish a silky texture.
Vegetables such as broccoli, carrots, and spinach increase the content of vitamins A, C, and K.
Home recipes allow control over salt and fat, making the meal healthier.
Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than traditional refined‑flour pasta.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates deliver sustained energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Added vegetables contribute vitamin C, folate, potassium, and antioxidants, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: A cream sauce made with low‑fat dairy or plant‑based alternatives supplies moderate amounts of mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats.

items.title: Plant‑based protein
items.content: Together, pasta and vegetables provide a decent amount of plant protein for tissue repair.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: High calorie content in cream sauce
items.content: Cream can add significant calories and saturated fat; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces or added salt can raise sodium; it is better to make the sauce from scratch with minimal salt.

items.title: Food safety with improper storage
items.content: Leaving the cooked dish at room temperature can promote bacterial growth; refrigerate within two hours and consume within 2 days.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Cook whole grain pasta in salted boiling water until al dente (about 8‑10 minutes). In a skillet, sauté diced vegetables (broccoli, carrots, spinach) until tender, add cream, simmer until thickened, season with salt, pepper, and herbs. Toss the pasta with the sauce, serve hot, and optionally garnish with grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Keep the cream sauce separate and reheat before serving. Frozen portions can be kept up to 1 month, though texture may change.

rice-white-with-corn-no-added-fat.title: Rice, white, with corn, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice with corn and no added fat is a ready‑to‑eat product composed of boiled white rice and whole corn kernels. It contains no added oils, making it low‑calorie and suitable for diet‑focused meals. The product is commonly used in school cafeterias, child nutrition programs, and as a quick side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rice‑corn combination provides a broader amino‑acid profile than each ingredient alone.
The white rice is steam‑cooked, preserving a high level of vitamin B1 (thiamine).
Corn adds natural sweetness and a bright yellow color without artificial dyes.
Zero added fat makes the product ideal for those monitoring fat and calorie intake.
It is frequently included in school nutrition programs to supply a balanced carbohydrate source.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice delivers quick‑digesting carbohydrates that fuel physical and mental activity.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: Corn contributes dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: The absence of added fats helps control overall caloric load and supports healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product provides B1, B3, and folate, which are essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Magnesium and phosphorus are present, important for bone health and muscle function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: The product is gluten‑free, but cross‑contamination can occur during manufacturing.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package. Serve it as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables, add it to soups, salads, or use it in child nutrition meals. For extra flavor, sprinkle fresh herbs or a light, low‑fat sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Szechuan Beef is a Chinese dish made from thin strips of beef quickly stir‑fried in a spicy sauce that combines soy sauce, chili, garlic, ginger, and the distinctive Szechuan peppercorns. The dish is known for its bold aroma, moderate heat, and the characteristic “numbing‑tingling” sensation from the peppercorns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally cooked in a wok over high heat to keep the beef crisp.
Szechuan peppercorns are actually berries that create a unique numbing effect, not true pepper.
Original recipes use a lean cut of beef so the sauce clings better to the meat.
Often served with steamed rice or noodles and vegetable sides such as broccoli or bell pepper.
Some regional variations add peanuts or toasted sesame seeds for extra crunch.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports normal hemoglobin levels and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins, especially B12, help maintain nervous system function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Szechuan pepper, ginger, and garlic are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Mild heat may aid digestion
items.content: Spicy foods can stimulate gastric secretions and promote faster digestion.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: Very hot dishes may cause heartburn or stomach irritation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some people are allergic to beef, which can manifest as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Szechuan peppercorns
items.content: People sensitive to Szechuan pepper may experience intense tingling or allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Szechuan Beef hot, either on its own or over steamed rice. Garnish with fresh herbs (cilantro, green onions) and sprinkle with toasted peanuts or sesame seeds for added texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftover Szechuan Beef in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it remains good for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.

content.title: About
content.content: A tomato sandwich on wheat consists of fresh slices of ripe tomatoes, lettuce leaves, mild cheese, and a light sauce placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread. It is a simple yet nutritious snack suitable for breakfast, lunch, or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that gives them their bright red color.
Wheat bread provides complex carbohydrates that help maintain steady energy levels.
The sandwich is easily customizable – add avocado, turkey, or hummus for variety.
Tomato sandwiches are a common offering in school and office cafeterias as a quick healthy option.
The combination of tomatoes and cheese enhances calcium absorption thanks to vitamin D found in many cheeses.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes provide a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread and vegetables supply fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie option
items.content: When portioned moderately, the sandwich is relatively low in calories, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Fiber and potassium from tomatoes contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may react to wheat bread.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces or salty cheese can raise sodium levels; choose low‑salt alternatives.

items.title: Tomato acidity
items.content: The acidity of tomatoes may cause heartburn or stomach discomfort in some individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Assemble the sandwich by layering tomato slices, lettuce, and cheese between the bread slices, then spread a light sauce (e.g., mustard or yogurt). It can be eaten immediately or wrapped for a portable snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Store bread in a dry place and tomatoes in the fridge to maintain freshness.
